documents.unit: Office of the University Provost (recommended language, hosted by School of Life Sciences Teaching and Learning Center)
documents.title: Syllabus and Policies for Generative AI (student considerations + Provost Recommended Language, three tiers)
tiers: Circumstantially permitted with explicit permission only
documents.summary: Provost-recommended syllabus language hosted by a School of Life Sciences teaching center. It gives students considerations on AI limits, citation and privacy, and offers three sample statements (generally permitted, permitted only for named assignments, not permitted) for instructors to pick from.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule; it says "each course has unique goals and values" so instructors must communicate expectations, and it supplies "three distinct approaches" of sample syllabus statements, so the decision is delegated to instructors with tiers listed.

units.why: States the university's purpose of balancing AI's learning potential against integrity, which is a framing principle for the guidance, hence P56 (institution-level preamble), informs.
units.anchor: balance the potential of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to support learning
units.frag_start: Arizona State University seeks to balance

units.why: "Because each course has unique goals and values" makes the AI rule a per-course choice by the instructor; P04 fits better than P83 because the unit is about who decides.
units.resolution_why: A wrote a normalized policy ('instructors set and communicate their own AI expectations') that adds 'set', which the sentence does not say; B left it null. The anchor states the reason, so null. Differences: policy (one coder wrote a normalized statement).
units.anchor: Because each course has unique goals and values
units.fit_note: Also links the choice to course goals (P83).

units.why: Instructors are told it is "essential" to communicate AI expectations in the syllabus, a duty to state the rule, so P09 and must.
units.resolution_why: A gave unit_stance neutral, B require. The sentence requires instructors to communicate, not students to use AI, so unit_stance is neutral (require would mean AI use is required). Differences: unit_stance (A=neutral, B=require).
units.anchor: instructors clearly communicate expectations for student use of generative AI in the syllabus
units.fit_note: Reads as 'essential' rather than a formal mandate.

units.why: 'Instructors may wish to share some or all of the following considerations with students' is advice to explain AI cautions to students, so P66.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. 'Instructors may wish to share some or all of the following considerations with students' advises instructors to pass on the considerations (P66). Kept.
units.anchor: Instructors may wish to share some or all of the following considerations with students.
units.fit_note: Advises sharing considerations rather than discussing reasons for course rules.

units.why: "Do not use AI if it does not align with the assignment's purpose" tells students to judge fit to the assignment's learning aim, so P83 and a restriction.
units.resolution_why: A coded must-not and B should-not for 'Do not use AI if it does not align with the assignment's purpose.' It is an imperative in student-facing considerations, so must-not. Differences: modality (A=must-not, B=should-not).
units.anchor: Do not use AI if it does not align with the assignment’s purpose.
units.fit_note: Frames fit with the assignment's purpose, not formal learning objectives.

units.why: 'Low-effort prompts often lead to low-quality results. Effective use requires thoughtful prompting and revision' is practical prompting advice, so P93.
units.resolution_why: A wrote a normalized policy, B left it null. The two sentences 'Low-effort prompts often lead to low-quality results. Effective use requires thoughtful prompting and revision.' are in the anchor, so null. Differences: policy (one coder wrote a normalized statement).
units.anchor: Effective use requires thoughtful prompting and revision.

units.why: 'Do not assume outputs are correct. Students are responsible for verifying facts, data, and sources' says AI can be inaccurate and students must verify, so P31.
units.resolution_why: A wrote a normalized policy joining 'Do not assume outputs are correct' with the verification duty; B anchored the duty alone. The anchor states the duty in the source's words, so policy is null. Differences: policy (one coder wrote a normalized statement).
units.anchor: Students are responsible for verifying facts, data, and sources using reliable references.

units.why: Students "are responsible for properly citing and acknowledging any use" is a disclosure duty, P24, must.
units.resolution_why: A gave unit_stance require, B permit. Citing and acknowledging is a condition on permitted use, not a requirement to use AI, so permit. Differences: unit_stance (A=require, B=permit).
units.anchor: Students are responsible for properly citing and acknowledging any use of generative AI.

units.why: The disclosure must say "how AI was used and what prompts were used", naming prompt detail, so P25 rather than plain P24 (the P24 duty is a separate unit).
units.resolution_why: A gave unit_stance require, B permit. Disclosure with prompts is a condition on use, so permit. Differences: unit_stance (A=require, B=permit).
units.anchor: Include a brief disclosure describing how AI was used and what prompts were used.

units.why: "Failure to do so may violate academic integrity policies" makes nondisclosure itself a violation, P28.
units.resolution_why: A gave unit_stance neutral, B restrict. 'Failure to do so may violate academic integrity policies' states a consequence of not disclosing and does not itself allow or ban use, so neutral. Differences: unit_stance (A=neutral, B=restrict); policy (one coder wrote a normalized statement).
units.anchor: Failure to do so may violate academic integrity policies.
units.policy: Failure to properly cite and disclose AI use, including how it was used and the prompts, may violate academic integrity policies.

units.why: States that prompt information "may be retained" by tools, the factual reason behind the privacy rule (P50, informs).
units.resolution_why: A coded actor student, B all. The sentence is in the student-facing considerations, so student. Differences: actor (A=student, B=all).
units.anchor: may be retained by some generative AI tools and service providers.

units.why: "Do not include personal, sensitive, or confidential information in AI prompts" protects data, P50, must-not.
units.anchor: Do not include personal, sensitive, or confidential information in AI prompts.

units.why: Students are told to "follow all ASU technology use guidelines and information security expectations", compliance with existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: follow all ASU technology use guidelines and information security expectations

units.why: "Adhere to all FERPA laws" requires compliance with law on student privacy, P77.
units.anchor: Adhere to all FERPA laws and expectations related to student privacy.

units.why: "Do not disclose proprietary code, research data" bars sharing sensitive material with AI; it is about confidential data (P50) rather than assignment specs (P20).
units.anchor: Do not disclose proprietary code, research data, or other information sensitive to ASU
units.fit_note: Covers proprietary code and research data, not assignment specs or the student's own code.

units.why: "Strongly encouraged to use ChatGPT Edu" which is free and secure, recommends the university-provided tool (P92, institution-wide, not course-specific P17).

The encouragement is one rule; the no-cost fact is coded separately (B15), so the anchor alone states this unit and policy is null. Differences: policy (one coder wrote a normalized statement).
units.anchor: Students, staff, and faculty are strongly encouraged to use ChatGPT Edu
units.frag_end: not used to train OpenAI’s models.
units.fit_note: Also states no-cost access and data protection (P50, P51). Also states data are not used to train OpenAI models.

units.why: 'Available to ASU students at no cost' addresses cost and access, so P51.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. 'available to ASU students at no cost through a university agreement' states free access (P51); A folded it into the encouragement unit. Kept as a separate rule.
units.anchor: available to ASU students at no cost through a university agreement
units.fit_note: Free access is stated as a fact, not a promise of alternatives.

units.resolution_why: A gave unit_stance require, B permit. 'You must inform the instructor when you have used an AI tool' is a disclosure condition on welcome use, so permit. Differences: unit_stance (A=require, B=permit).
units.anchor: You must inform the instructor when you have used an AI tool.

units.resolution_why: A coded phase during-work, B when-misuse. The sentence says what will be 'assumed' about work that does not articulate AI use, a consequence of nondisclosure, so when-misuse. unit_stance neutral (A) since it states an assumption. Differences: phase (A=during-work, B=when-misuse); unit_stance (A=neutral, B=restrict).

'Using AI tools to generate content without proper acknowledgement will be considered a violation' forbids unacknowledged use within a tier that welcomes AI, so must-not and restrict. Differences: modality (A=informs, B=must-not); unit_stance (A=prohibit, B=restrict).

units.resolution_why: A wrote a normalized policy, B left it null. The anchor alone cuts off before the instructor's duty, and A's statement follows the source ('The instructor will provide specific instructions on how to utilize generative AI tools for these assignments, as well as how to include appropriate attribution') without adding to it, so A's policy stands. documents.summary: The Provost page describes ASU's tools (CreateAI Builder, ChatGPT EDU), encourages faculty to build AI into teaching, and gives account and data cautions for faculty. It is mostly platform description with little rule text.

documents.title: AI MS Handbook 2026-2027
documents.summary: The AI MS handbook has a single AI rule in its academic integrity section: generative AI on any assignment or exam is academic dishonesty unless the instructor explicitly allows it, with sanctions under university and school guidelines.
documents.stance_why: The handbook says "Unless explicitly allowed by your instructor, using generative AI tools to complete any portion of a course assignment or exam will be considered academic dishonesty", so AI is banned unless permitted, which is restrict.
